claim: An arabinan-containing polysaccharide was isolated from pea fiber.
source: To illustrate one approach, an arabinan-containing polysaccharide was isolated from pea fiber, its structure defined, and forward genetic and proteomic analyses used to compare its effects, versus unfractionated pea fiber and sugar beet arabinan, on a human gut bacterial strain consortium in gnotobiotic mice.
evidence: The manuscript describes the isolation procedure and structural characterization of the arabinan-containing polysaccharide from pea fiber in the Methods and Results sections.

claim: Forward genetic and proteomic analyses were used to compare the effects of pea fiber arabinan versus unfractionated pea fiber and sugar beet arabinan on a human gut bacterial strain consortium in gnotobiotic mice.
source: To illustrate one approach, an arabinan-containing polysaccharide was isolated from pea fiber, its structure defined, and forward genetic and proteomic analyses used to compare its effects, versus unfractionated pea fiber and sugar beet arabinan, on a human gut bacterial strain consortium in gnotobiotic mice.
evidence: The manuscript presents data from INSeq (forward genetic analysis) and metaproteomic analysis comparing the effects of these different fiber preparations.

claim: Three MFABs, each containing a unique glycan/fluorophore combination, were simultaneously orally gavaged into gnotobiotic mice.
source: Three MFABs, each containing a unique glycan/fluorophore combination, were simultaneously orally gavaged into gnotobiotic mice, recovered from their intestines, and analyzed to directly quantify bacterial metabolism of structurally distinct arabinans in different human diet contexts.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental procedure where multiple MFAB types were administered to mice and subsequently recovered.

claim: MFABs were recovered from mouse intestines and analyzed to directly quantify bacterial metabolism of structurally distinct arabinans in different human diet contexts.
source: Three MFABs, each containing a unique glycan/fluorophore combination, were simultaneously orally gavaged into gnotobiotic mice, recovered from their intestines, and analyzed to directly quantify bacterial metabolism of structurally distinct arabinans in different human diet contexts.
evidence: The manuscript presents quantitative data on polysaccharide degradation from recovered beads under different dietary conditions.

claim: Colocalizing pea-fiber arabinan and glucomannan on the bead surface enhanced in vivo degradation of glucomannan.
source: Colocalizing pea-fiber arabinan and another polysaccharide (glucomannan) on the bead surface enhanced in vivo degradation of glucomannan.
evidence: Figure 5D shows significantly more glucomannan was degraded when colocalized with PFABN on beads in mice receiving pea fiber-supplemented diet compared to glucomannan alone.

claim: The gut microbiota is complex and dynamic and exhibits considerable intra- and interpersonal variation in its configurations.
source: The gut microbiota is complex and dynamic and exhibits considerable intra- and interpersonal variation in its configurations (Lloyd-Price et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lloyd-Price et al., 2017.

claim: Methods of food processing affect the representation of bioactive food components.
source: Furthermore, much needs to be learned about the effects of current methods of food processing on the representation of bioactive food components (Carmody et al., 2015; Wolf et al., 2019), and about the mechanisms that determine whether and how microbes compete and/or cooperate for them.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Carmody et al., 2015 and Wolf et al., 2019.

claim: Plant fibers are complex mixtures of biomolecules whose composition varies depending upon their source, method of initial recovery, and the food processing techniques used.
source: Plant fibers are complex mixtures of biomolecules whose composition varies depending upon their source, method of initial recovery, and the food processing techniques used to incorporate them into food products that have satisfactory organoleptic properties (texture, taste, smell) (Shahidi and Ho, 1998; Caffall and Mohnen, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Shahidi and Ho, 1998 and Caffall and Mohnen, 2009.

claim: Plant fibers are composed of but not limited to polysaccharides, proteins, fatty acids, polyphenols, and other plant-derived small molecules.
source: Plant fibers are composed of but not limited to polysaccharides, proteins, fatty acids, polyphenols, and other plant-derived small molecules (Nicholson et al., 2012; Scalbert et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nicholson et al., 2012 and Scalbert et al., 2014.

claim: Knowledge of the genetic underpinnings of how various members of the gut microbiota recognize and metabolize glycans has increased substantially in recent years.
source: Nonetheless, knowledge of the genetic underpinnings of how various members of the gut microbiota recognize and metabolize glycans has increased substantially in recent years through a combination of in vitro and in vivo approaches (Brown and Koropatkin, 2020; Kaoutari et al., 2013; Ndeh and Gilbert, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Brown and Koropatkin, 2020; Kaoutari et al., 2013; and Ndeh and Gilbert, 2018.

claim: Having a suitable complement of genes for acquiring and processing a given glycan structure in vitro does not necessarily predict whether that organism will be a consumer in vivo.
source: Knowing that a given microbiota member has a suitable complement of genes for acquiring and processing a given glycan structure in vitro does not necessarily predict whether that organism will be a consumer in vivo (Flint et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Flint et al., 2015.

claim: Pea fiber was selected based on results obtained from a screen of 34 types of food-grade crude plant fibers.
source: Pea fiber was selected based on results obtained from a screen we conducted of 34 types of food-grade crude plant fibers obtained from various sources, including the byproducts of food manufacturing (Patnode et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Patnode et al., 2019.

claim: The screen was performed in gnotobiotic mice colonized with a defined consortium of cultured sequenced human gut bacterial strains, including several saccharolytic Bacteroides species.
source: The screen was performed in gnotobiotic mice colonized with a defined consortium of cultured sequenced human gut bacterial strains, including several saccharolytic Bacteroides species.
evidence: This describes the experimental design used in the referenced screening study.

claim: Supplementation of the HiSF-LoFV diet with fiber generated from the seed coat of the pea, Pisum sativum, produced a significant increase in the abundance of Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron.
source: Supplementation of this 'HiSF-LoFV' diet with fiber generated from the seed coat of the pea, Pisum sativum, produced a significant increase in the abundance of Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (Patnode et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Patnode et al., 2019.

claim: The isolated pea fiber fraction (fraction 8; 4M KOH) possessed high carbohydrate and low protein content, high monosaccharide diversity, and a high relative proportion of arabinose.
source: The fraction isolated under the harshest conditions (fraction 8; 4M KOH) possessed high carbohydrate and low protein content, high monosaccharide diversity, and a high relative proportion of arabinose.
evidence: This is based on analytical characterization data presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The mole percent representation of arabinose in the isolated pea fiber arabinan was 71%.
source: The mole percent representation of arabinose in the end product was 71% (corresponding values for xylose, galactose, and glucose were 12%, 11% and 6%, respectively) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on GC-MS analysis of monosaccharide composition shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Glycosyl-linkage analysis of the isolated glycan revealed a 2-O-branched arabinan attached to small rhamnogalacturonan-I (RGI) pectic fragments and small galactan oligomers.
source: Glycosyl-linkage analysis of the isolated glycan revealed a 2-O-branched arabinan (5-substituted arabinose, 2,5-substituted arabinose, 2,3,5-substituted arabinose) (Figure 1B) attached to small rhamnogalacturonan-I (RGI) pectic fragments (2-substituted and 2,4-substituted rhamnose) and small galactan oligomers (4-substituted galactose) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on glycosyl-linkage analysis data presented in Figure 1B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Approximately 90% of all non-starch carbohydrate in PFABN is represented by what is likely a single species of polysaccharide, with the remaining being xylan.
source: We named the isolated polysaccharide fraction 'pea fiber arabinan' (PFABN) based on (1) these linkage results, (2) the fact that arabinose comprises the majority of its monosaccharide content (71 mole percent), and (3) our observation that ~90% of all non-starch carbohydrate is represented by what is likely a single species of polysaccharide, with the remaining being xylan.
evidence: This is based on the authors' analysis of the linkage and monosaccharide composition data.

claim: Sugar beet arabinan (SBABN) is primarily 3-O-branched.
source: Unlike PFABN, sugar beet arabinan (SBABN) is primarily 3-O-branched as revealed by glycosyl-linkage analysis (Figure 1B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on glycosyl-linkage analysis data presented in Figure 1B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: PFABN contains twofold more triply branched 2,3,5-substituted arabinose monomers than SBABN.
source: PFABN also contains twofold more triply branched 2,3,5-substituted arabinose monomers, suggesting it is more sterically encumbered than SBABN.
evidence: This is based on comparison of glycosyl-linkage analysis data for PFABN and SBABN.

claim: PFABN is more sterically encumbered than SBABN.
source: PFABN also contains twofold more triply branched 2,3,5-substituted arabinose monomers, suggesting it is more sterically encumbered than SBABN.
evidence: This is inferred from the higher content of triply branched arabinose monomers in PFABN.

claim: B. ovatus ATCC 8483, B. cellulosilyticus WH2, and B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482 grew on isolated PFABN and SBABN, although less rapidly during the exponential phase of growth and to a lower cell density than in medium containing an equivalent concentration of d-glucose.
source: In vitro assays performed in a minimal defined medium (McNulty et al., 2013) with Bacteroides type strains established that B. ovatus ATCC 8483, B. cellulosilyticus WH2, and B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482 grew on isolated PFABN and SBABN, although less rapidly during the exponential phase of growth and to a lower cell density than in medium containing an equivalent concentration of d-glucose (results based on measurements of OD600; see Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on in vitro growth assays shown in Figure 1C.

claim: B. vulgatus ATCC 8482 grew as rapidly or faster and to the same or higher density on PFABN and SBABN, respectively, compared to d-glucose.
source: In contrast, B. vulgatus ATCC 8482 grew as rapidly or faster and to the same or higher density on PFABN and SBABN, respectively, compared to d-glucose (p<0.05, one-way analysis of variance [ANOVA] with Tukey's honest significant difference, FDR corrected).
evidence: This is based on in vitro growth assays with statistical analysis.

claim: B. vulgatus ATCC 8482 reached exponential growth more quickly on PFABN and SBABN than when d-glucose was present in the medium.
source: B. vulgatus ATCC 8482 also reached exponential growth more quickly than when d-glucose was present in this medium (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on in vitro growth assays shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The 14-member consortium contained 58,537 known or predicted protein-coding genes.
source: Adult germ-free C57Bl/6J mice were colonized with a 14-member consortium of sequenced bacterial strains containing 58,537 known or predicted protein-coding genes.
evidence: This is based on genomic analysis of the bacterial strains in the consortium.

claim: Five of the Bacteroides were each represented by previously described libraries of tens of thousands of transposon (Tn) insertion mutants.
source: Five of the Bacteroides (B. thetaiotaomicron strains VPI-5482 and 7330, B. vulgatus ATCC 8482, B. cellulosilyticus WH2, B. ovatus ATCC 8483) were each represented by previously described libraries of tens of thousands of transposon (Tn) insertion mutants (Hibberd et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hibberd et al., 2017 and Wu et al., 2015.

claim: The overall change in abundance of each mutant library in response to various diet manipulations was similar to the corresponding parental wild-type strain.
source: These studies had shown that collectively the overall change in abundance of each mutant library in response to various diet manipulations was similar to the corresponding parental wild-type strain.
evidence: This is based on previous studies cited (Hibberd et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2015).

claim: B. thetaiotaomicron 7330 failed to colonize mice at levels above a (relative) abundance of 0.1% under any of the diet conditions tested.
source: Of the 14-member consortium, only B. thetaiotaomicron 7330 failed to colonize mice at levels above a (relative) abundance of 0.1% under any of the diet conditions tested.
evidence: This is based on community profiling data from the experiments.

claim: B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482 responded to all three supplements (pea fiber, PFABN, and SBABN).
source: Five community members exhibited statistically significant, albeit distinct, differences in their absolute abundances in response to specific glycan preparations: (1) B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482 responded to all three supplements
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of community profiling data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: B. ovatus ATCC 8483 increased after exposure to both intact pea fiber and PFABN but not to SBABN.
source: (2) B. ovatus ATCC 8483 increased after exposure to both intact pea fiber and PFABN but not to SBABN
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of community profiling data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: B. vulgatus ATCC 8482 exhibited significant increases with SBABN.
source: (3) B. vulgatus ATCC 8482 exhibited significant increases with SBABN
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of community profiling data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: B. cellulosilyticus WH2 and Ruminococcaceae sp. TSDC 17.2 increased significantly when exposed to intact pea fiber but not to either of the isolated arabinan preparations.
source: (4) B. cellulosilyticus WH2 and Ruminococcaceae sp. TSDC 17.2 increased significantly when exposed to intact pea fiber but not to either of the isolated arabinan preparations (Figure 2B, Supplementary file 2) (p<0.01, generalized linear mixed-effects model [Gaussian]; two-way ANOVA with Tukey's HSD, FDR corrected).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of community profiling data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Both isolated arabinan preparations had a significantly greater specific activity compared to intact pea fiber at the doses tested.
source: This metric of specific activity, which takes into account the absolute mass of supplement consumed daily by members of the different groups of mice, revealed that both of the isolated arabinan preparations had a significantly greater effect compared to intact pea fiber at the doses tested (Figure 2C) (p<0.05 mixed-effects linear model [Gaussian]; one-way ANOVA with Tukey's honest significant difference, FDR corrected).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of specific activity data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Bacteroides spp. possess multiple polysaccharide utilization loci (PULs).
source: Bacteroides spp. possess multiple polysaccharide utilization loci (PULs); a shared feature of PULs is an adjacent pair of susC and susD homologs responsible for binding extracellular polysaccharide fragments and importing them into the periplasm.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Bacteroides species.

claim: A shared feature of PULs is an adjacent pair of susC and susD homologs responsible for binding extracellular polysaccharide fragments and importing them into the periplasm.
source: Bacteroides spp. possess multiple polysaccharide utilization loci (PULs); a shared feature of PULs is an adjacent pair of susC and susD homologs responsible for binding extracellular polysaccharide fragments and importing them into the periplasm.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PUL structure and function.

claim: PUL genes encode various carbohydrate active enzymes (CAZymes) involved in polysaccharide depolymerization.
source: PUL genes also encode various carbohydrate active enzymes (CAZymes) involved in polysaccharide depolymerization, as well as transcriptional regulators that allow the locus to be induced in the presence of glycans it can recognize/utilize (Anderson and Salyers, 1989; Terrapon et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Anderson and Salyers, 1989 and Terrapon et al., 2018.

claim: Regulated expression of PULs allows bacteria to acquire nutrients within the highly competitive environment of the gut.
source: Regulated expression of PULs allows bacteria to acquire nutrients within the highly competitive environment of the gut (Martens et al., 2011; Tuncil et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Martens et al., 2011 and Tuncil et al., 2017.

claim: 14, 12, 11, and 8 PULs were identified as responsive to at least one of the diet supplements in B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482, B. ovatus ATCC 8483, B. cellulosilyticus WH2, and B. vulgatus ATCC 8482, respectively.
source: Based on gene set enrichment analysis (Luo et al., 2009), we identified 14, 12, 11, and 8 PULs that we deemed 'responsive' to at least one of the diet supplements in B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482 (BT), B. ovatus ATCC 8483 (Bovatus), B. cellulosilyticus WH2 (BcellWH2), and B. vulgatus ATCC 8482 (BVU), respectively (adjusted p-value<0.05, unpaired one-sample Z-test, FDR-corrected).
evidence: This is based on gene set enrichment analysis of metaproteomic data.

claim: The fitness scores of a total of 39 genes in B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482, 135 genes in B. ovatus ATCC 8483, 346 genes in B. cellulosilyticus WH2, and 82 genes in B. vulgatus ATCC 8482 were significantly decreased during diet supplementation with either pea fiber, PFABN, or SBABN.
source: The results disclosed that the fitness scores of a total of 39 genes in B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482, 135 genes in B. ovatus ATCC 8483, 346 genes in B. cellulosilyticus WH2, and 82 genes in B. vulgatus ATCC 8482 were significantly decreased during diet supplementation with either pea fiber, PFABN, or SBABN (Supplementary file 4) (adjusted p-value<0.05, FDR corrected).
evidence: This is based on INSeq analysis of transposon mutant libraries.

claim: PFABN is a key bioactive component of pea fiber utilized by B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482, B. vulgatus ATCC 8482, B. cellulosilyticus WH2, and B. ovatus ATCC 8483.
source: Together, these community configurational and functional responses to diet supplementation provided evidence that PFABN is a key bioactive component of pea fiber utilized by B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482, B. vulgatus ATCC 8482, B. cellulosilyticus WH2, and B. ovatus ATCC 8483.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined community profiling, metaproteomic, and INSeq data.

claim: Amine plus phosphonate functionalized beads contain 2.18 × 10^10 ± 3.49 × 10^9 reactive amines per bead.
source: The results revealed that amine plus phosphonate functionalized beads contain 2.18 × 1010 ± 3.49 × 109 (mean ± s.d.) reactive amines per bead versus 1.20 × 109 ± 1.92 × 108 reactive amines after surface acetylation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on ninhydrin-based colorimetric assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Streptavidin-coated beads possess 23-fold fewer potential binding sites than amine plus phosphonate functionalized beads.
source: By comparison, streptavidin-coated beads used in our previously published procedure (Patnode et al., 2019) possess 23-fold fewer potential binding sites (9.21 × 108 ± 1.13 × 108 molecules of biotin per bead).
evidence: This is based on comparison of quantified binding sites between the two bead types.

claim: Incubation with a combination of endo-arabinanase and α-l-arabinofuranosidase enzymes removed 88 ± 1.2% of the immobilized PFABN after 30 min.
source: Incubation with a combination of endo-arabinanase and α-l-arabinofuranosidase enzymes removed 88 ± 1.2% (mean ± s.d.) of the immobilized PFABN after 30 min while incubation with each enzyme individually removed greater than 80% of the glycan after 30 min and more than 90% after 20 hr.
evidence: This is based on in vitro enzyme degradation assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: An endo-inulinase with specificity toward β(1-2)-linked fructose resides failed to degrade PFABN.
source: In contrast, an endo-inulinase with specificity toward β(1-2)-linked fructose resides failed to degrade PFABN (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on in vitro enzyme degradation assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Added PFABN was required for degradation of immobilized PFABN from beads by B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482 and B. cellulosilyticus WH2 in vitro.
source: Under the conditions tested, added PFABN was required for degradation of immobilized PFABN from beads; the amount of PFABN removed from the bead surface increased with increasing incubation time, with maximum values of 64 ± 9% (mean ± s.d.) and 48 ± 3% achieved with B. thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482 and B. cellulosilyticus WH2, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on in vitro bacterial degradation assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The quantities of neutral monosaccharides liberated by acid hydrolysis from the surfaces of beads recovered from the cecums of germ-free mice were not significantly different from the amounts liberated from the input bead preparations with one exception.
source: The quantities of neutral monosaccharides liberated by acid hydrolysis from the surfaces of beads recovered from the cecums of germ-free mice were not significantly different from the amounts liberated from the input bead preparations with one exception – a slight, albeit statistically significant, increase in galactose from beads coated with PFABN and SBABN (Figure 4—figure supplement 3; p<0.05, Mann–Whitney U test).
evidence: This is based on GC-MS analysis of beads recovered from germ-free mice shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The mass of arabinose was significantly decreased when PFABN- or SBABN-coated beads were recovered from colonized mice fed the unsupplemented HiSF-LoFV diet.
source: In contrast to germ-free controls (see Figure 4—figure supplement 3), the mass of arabinose was significantly decreased when PFABN- or SBABN-coated beads were recovered from colonized mice fed the unsupplemented HiSF-LoFV diet (Figure 4B,C; p<0.05, Mann–Whitney U test).
evidence: This is based on GC-MS analysis of beads recovered from colonized mice shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: Supplementation with unfractionated pea fiber induced a community configuration associated with significantly increased capacity to degrade both PFABN and SBABN.
source: Compared to the base HiSF-LoFV diet, supplementation with unfractionated pea fiber induced a community configuration associated with significantly increased capacity to degrade both PFABN and SBABN as judged by the amount of arabinose remaining on recovered beads (Figure 4B,C; p<0.05, Mann–Whitney U test).
evidence: This is based on GC-MS analysis of beads recovered from colonized mice shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: Loss of arabinose from either PFABN- or SBABN-beads was not significantly different between the two bead types when the HiSF-LoFV diet was supplemented with either of these isolated arabinan preparations.
source: Loss of arabinose from either PFABN- or SBABN-beads was not significantly different between the two bead types when the HiSF-LoFV diet was supplemented with either of these isolated arabinan preparations, demonstrating functional equivalence in the capacity of each community to utilize either arabinan (see Figure 4B,C and Supplementary file 5 which provides evidence that results from cecal samples [Experiment 1] and fecal samples [Experiment 2] were comparable).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of bead degradation data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: Xylan was more efficiently processed by the microbiota in all three supplemented diet contexts.
source: Beads coated in PFABN revealed that xylan (xylose monosaccharide remaining on PFABN beads) was more efficiently processed by the microbiota in all three supplemented diet contexts (Figure 4B; p<0.05, Mann–Whitney U test).
evidence: This is based on GC-MS analysis of xylose remaining on beads shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The galactan content from both arabinan preparations was not utilized under any of the diet conditions tested.
source: In contrast to xylan, the galactan content from both arabinan preparations was not utilized under any of the diet conditions tested (Figure 4B,C and Supplementary file 5), suggesting that β(1-4) galactan degradation in vivo has lower priority compared to the available arabinan (Tuncil et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on GC-MS analysis of galactose remaining on beads shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: β(1-4) galactan degradation in vivo has lower priority compared to the available arabinan.
source: In contrast to xylan, the galactan content from both arabinan preparations was not utilized under any of the diet conditions tested (Figure 4B,C and Supplementary file 5), suggesting that β(1-4) galactan degradation in vivo has lower priority compared to the available arabinan (Tuncil et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of galactan degradation and supported by citation to Tuncil et al., 2017.

claim: Among the pea fiber-responsive Bacteroides, only B. ovatus ATCC 8483 and B. cellulosilyticus WH2 were able to grow in minimal medium containing glucomannan as the sole carbon source.
source: We found that among the pea fiber-responsive Bacteroides identified above, only B. ovatus ATCC 8483 and B. cellulosilyticus WH2 were able to grow in minimal medium containing glucomannan as the sole carbon source (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is based on in vitro growth assays shown in Figure 5A.

claim: B. ovatus ATCC 8483 and B. cellulosilyticus WH2 have PULs known to be induced by glucomannan in vitro.
source: Both organisms have PULs known to be induced by glucomannan in vitro (PUL28 in B. cellulosilyticus WH2; PULs 52 and 80 in B. ovatus ATCC 8483); each of these PULs encodes at least one GH26 enzyme with β-mannanase activity (Bågenholm et al., 2017; Martens et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bågenholm et al., 2017 and Martens et al., 2011.

claim: Glucomannan on beads coated with glucomannan alone was degraded to a similar extent in mice receiving the unsupplemented or pea fiber-supplemented HiSF-LoFV diets.
source: The results revealed that glucomannan on beads coated with glucomannan alone was degraded to a similar extent in mice receiving the unsupplemented or pea fiber-supplemented HiSF-LoFV diets (Figure 5D and Supplementary file 5; p=0.87, Mann–Whitney U test).
evidence: This is based on GC-MS analysis of beads recovered from mice shown in Figure 5D.

claim: When presented with PFABN on the same bead, significantly more glucomannan was degraded by the microbiota of mice receiving the pea fiber-supplemented diet as compared to the unsupplemented diet.
source: However, when presented with PFABN on the same bead, significantly more glucomannan was degraded by the microbiota of mice receiving the pea fiber-supplemented diet as compared to the unsupplemented diet (Figure 5D; p<0.05, Mann–Whitney U test).
evidence: This is based on GC-MS analysis of beads recovered from mice shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The amount of arabinose remaining on beads coated with PFABN and glucomannan, and PFABN alone, was significantly reduced with pea fiber supplementation.
source: The amount of arabinose remaining on beads coated with PFABN and glucomannan, and PFABN alone, was also significantly reduced (degradation increased) with pea fiber supplementation (Figure 5D; p<0.05, Mann–Whitney U test).
evidence: This is based on GC-MS analysis of beads recovered from mice shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Deliberate physical colocalization can result in quantitatively modest, albeit statistically significant synergistic degradation of polysaccharides during fiber supplementation.
source: These results show that deliberate physical colocalization can result in quantitatively modest, albeit statistically significant synergistic degradation of polysaccharides during fiber supplementation (Supplementary file 5; p<0.05, linear model; diet supplement by bead-type interaction term).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of bead degradation data showing a significant interaction effect.

claim: The specific activity of each isolated arabinan was superior to unfractionated pea fiber.
source: The specific activity of each isolated arabinan (in this case the increase in absolute abundance of the responsive Bacteroides per unit mass of diet ingredient consumed per day) was superior to unfractionated pea fiber (Figure 2C), emphasizing, as others have, the importance of characterizing the effects of plant fibers on both the microbiota and host in order to inform future studies at the intersection of food science, nutrition, and human microbial ecology research (Gidley and Yakubov, 2019).
evidence: This is based on specific activity calculations shown in Figure 2C and supported by citation to Gidley and Yakubov, 2019.

claim: MFABs represent a technology for measuring biochemical activities expressed by a microbial community of interest in vivo or ex vivo.
source: The bead-based MFABs described in this report represent a technology for measuring biochemical activities expressed by a microbial community of interest in vivo or ex vivo.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the utility of the MFAB technology demonstrated in the manuscript.

claim: A typical gavage of 10^7 beads contained 100 µg of bead-immobilized polysaccharide, 1000 times less polysaccharide than was consumed daily in the diet by mice in the polysaccharide-supplemented arms of the experiments.
source: Determining the latter is challenging in our animal model; a typical gavage of 107 beads contained 100 µg of bead-immobilized polysaccharide, 1000 times more polysaccharide was consumed daily in the diet by mice in the polysaccharide-supplemented arms of our experiments.
evidence: This is based on calculations of polysaccharide amounts on beads versus in the diet.

claim: MFABs possess a greater number of sites for ligand attachment than streptavidin-coated beads.
source: By immobilizing ligand directly on the bead surface, MFABs possess a greater number of sites for ligand attachment than streptavidin-coated beads and include no protein constituents.
evidence: This is based on quantification of binding sites on both bead types.

claim: Higher ligand density enables higher levels of ligand loading, which reduces the absolute number of beads that need to be administered, recovered, and processed, and increases the dynamic range of a functional activity readout.
source: Higher ligand density enables higher levels of ligand loading, which reduces the absolute number of beads that need to be administered, recovered, and processed, and increases the dynamic range of a functional activity readout.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the higher ligand density of MFABs.

claim: The absolute abundances of B. cellulosilyticus WH2 and Ruminococcaceae sp. TSDC 17.2 increase significantly when animals were consuming the crude pea fiber-supplemented diet, but not during supplementation with either of the isolated arabinans.
source: We found that the absolute abundances of B. cellulosilyticus WH2 and Ruminococcaceae sp. TSDC 17.2 increase significantly when animals were consuming the crude pea fiber-supplemented diet, but not during supplementation with either of the isolated arabinans.
evidence: This is based on community profiling data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The chemistry for covalent polysaccharide attachment to MFABs allows for dense ligand presentation.
source: The chemistry for covalent polysaccharide attachment to MFABs not only allows for dense ligand presentation, but also enables multiple ligands to be simultaneously immobilized to create 'hybrid' beads to model the effects of physical colocalization of different fiber components on microbial degradation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the successful creation of beads with multiple polysaccharides.

claim: The chemistry for covalent polysaccharide attachment to MFABs enables multiple ligands to be simultaneously immobilized to create 'hybrid' beads.
source: The chemistry for covalent polysaccharide attachment to MFABs not only allows for dense ligand presentation, but also enables multiple ligands to be simultaneously immobilized to create 'hybrid' beads to model the effects of physical colocalization of different fiber components on microbial degradation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the successful creation of beads with both PFABN and glucomannan.

claim: Crude plant fibers contain various polysaccharides densely intercalated within a cellulose-lignin matrix.
source: Crude plant fibers contain various polysaccharides densely intercalated within a cellulose-lignin matrix (Caffall and Mohnen, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Caffall and Mohnen, 2009.

claim: The HiSF-LoFV diet was formulated to represent the upper tertile of saturated fat consumption and lower tertile of fruit and vegetable consumption by individuals living in the USA, as reported in the NHANES database.
source: Mice were fed a low-fiber diet formulated to represent the upper tertile of saturated fat consumption and lower tertile of fruit and vegetable consumption by individuals living in the USA, as reported in the NHANES database (Ridaura et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ridaura et al., 2013.

claim: The procedure for isolating PFABN from pea fiber is scalable.
source: We subsequently developed a scalable abbreviated procedure for preparing this fraction from pea fiber (see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript describes isolation of 51 g of PFABN with 22% overall yield.

claim: The overall yield of PFABN isolation was 22%.
source: The entire procedure was repeated five times to isolate 51 g of PFABN (overall yield 22%).
evidence: This is based on the mass of starting material and final product.

claim: Bead fluorescence could be modulated over four orders of magnitude by titration of the reactant fluorophore.
source: Fluorophore coupling was specific to beads with surface amines (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C). Bead fluorescence could be modulated over four orders of magnitude simply by titration of the reactant fluorophore (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is based on fluorescence measurements shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Adding 0.2 mg of CDAP per mg polysaccharide resulted in consistent and specific SBABN immobilization without ligand overactivation.
source: Using SBABN as a test case, we found that adding 0.2 mg of CDAP per mg polysaccharide resulted in consistent and specific SBABN immobilization without ligand overactivation (manifested by aggregation and carbamoylation of hydroxyl groups) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on optimization experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Levels of conjugation ranged from 2 to 20 ng of arabinose per 1000 beads when immobilizing SBABN.
source: Throughout our experiments, levels of conjugation ranged from 2 to 20 ng of arabinose per 1000 beads when immobilizing SBABN.
evidence: This is based on GC-MS quantification of arabinose on beads across multiple experiments.

claim: Maltodextrin conjugation resulted in 4.43 ± 1.03 ng of immobilized glucose per 1000 beads or 2.05 × 10^9 molecules of maltodextrin per bead.
source: Conjugation resulted in 4.43 ± 1.03 ng of immobilized glucose per 1000 beads or 2.05 × 109 molecules of maltodextrin per bead (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C); this represents 9.4% of all available surface reactive amines.
evidence: This is based on GC-MS quantification of glucose on beads shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Maltodextrin conjugation represents 9.4% of all available surface reactive amines.
source: Conjugation resulted in 4.43 ± 1.03 ng of immobilized glucose per 1000 beads or 2.05 × 109 molecules of maltodextrin per bead (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C); this represents 9.4% of all available surface reactive amines.
evidence: This is calculated from the number of maltodextrin molecules per bead and the number of reactive amines per bead.

claim: The procedure typically recovers 20–50% of the input beads from the cecum 4 hr post-gavage.
source: The procedure described above typically recovers 20–50% of the input beads from the cecum 4 hr post-gavage.
evidence: This is based on bead recovery data from multiple experiments.

claim: Bead purity after FACS sorting typically exceeded 98%.
source: Aliquots of input beads were sorted throughout the procedure to quantify and monitor sort yield and purity. Bead purity typically exceeded 98%.
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis of sorted beads.

claim: SDS is widely used as a detergent in protein extraction protocols for its increased efficiency of whole-cell protein solubilization.
source: SDS is widely used as a detergent in protein extraction protocols for its increased efficiency of whole-cell protein solubilization.
evidence: This is established knowledge about SDS use in protein extraction.

claim: Inclusion of SDS in protein extraction protocols increases peptide identification rates from a wide range of proteins, including peptides found in membrane-associated proteins.
source: A number of proteome publications have demonstrated that inclusion of this detergent in protein extraction protocols increases peptide identification rates from a wide range of proteins, including peptides found in membrane-associated proteins (Tanca et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tanca et al., 2013.

claim: Inclusion of SDS in the extraction method increases total peptide identifications, including membrane protein representation.
source: We have also documented an increase in total peptide identifications, including membrane protein representation, after inclusion of SDS in the extraction method that we have applied to a variety of microbial systems (Blakeley-Ruiz et al., 2019; Nickels et al., 2020; Salvachúa et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Blakeley-Ruiz et al., 2019; Nickels et al., 2020; and Salvachúa et al., 2020.
